intro: Take our free B2 English mock test to check your level before a Skilled Worker visa application. Answer grammar, reading and listening questions at upper-intermediate level, see your score instantly, and practise the speaking tasks.

sections.heading: About this B2 English mock test
sections.text:
Each B2 English mock test has 24 questions in three parts:
- Part 1: 12 grammar and vocabulary questions
- Part 2: two longer texts to read, with 3 questions each
- Part 3: two recordings to listen to, with 3 questions each

Your browser reads the recordings aloud, and you can listen twice. When you finish, you see your score for each part and an explanation for every question you missed. Questions are chosen at random, so every mock test is different.

Below the test there are speaking tasks with a timer, at the level you’ll need in a real test.

sections.heading: Who needs B2 English?
sections.text:
Since 8 January 2026, you need English at B2 level for:
- the [Skilled Worker visa](/skilled-worker-visa-formally-tier-t2-general/), if you’re applying for the first time
- the Scale-up and High Potential Individual visas

If your last visa was a Skilled Worker visa granted at B1, you can usually stay at B1 when you extend or change employer.

B2 is also due to become the level for settlement. From 26 March 2027, most people applying for [Indefinite Leave to Remain](/indefinite-leave-to-remain-ilr/) will need B2 instead of B1. For citizenship and ILR before then, try our [B1 English mock test](/b1-english-mock-test/).

sections.heading: What B2 level means
sections.text:
B2, or upper-intermediate, is the fourth of six CEFR levels. At B2 you can:
- understand the main ideas of complex texts, including technical discussions in your own field
- follow news reports, talks and conversations at normal speed
- speak fluently enough to talk with native speakers without strain on either side
- explain a viewpoint, giving the advantages and disadvantages of different options

The step up from B1 is mostly about range: more vocabulary, more complex grammar and longer, better-organised answers.

sections.heading: Ways to prove your English
sections.text:
Our B2 English mock test is for practice. For a Skilled Worker visa, you can prove your English by:
- passing a Secure English Language Test (SELT) at B2 or above, from a Home Office approved provider, covering reading, writing, speaking and listening
- having a degree taught in English, confirmed by Ecctis if it’s from outside the UK
- being a national of a majority English-speaking country
- having a GCSE, A level or Scottish Higher in English, gained at school in the UK while under 18

See the [official list of approved tests on GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/prove-your-english-language-abilities-with-a-secure-english-language-test-selt) before you book. Results from other tests aren’t accepted.

sections.heading: Tips to reach B2
sections.text:
- Read news articles and reports in English every day, and note useful phrases.
- Listen to podcasts or radio at normal speed, without subtitles.
- Practise linking ideas with words like however, although, whereas and as a result.
- Write short opinion pieces and ask someone to check them.
- Take our B2 English mock test regularly and aim for 18 or more out of 24 before you book a real test.

faqs.q: Is the B2 English mock test free?
faqs.a: Yes, free and with no sign-up. Take it as often as you like.

faqs.q: Is this an official English test?
faqs.a: No. It’s a practice check written by us. Your visa application needs a Secure English Language Test from a Home Office approved provider, unless you’re exempt or have another way to prove your English.

faqs.q: Do I need B2 English for a Skilled Worker visa?
faqs.a: Yes, if you’re applying for the first time on or after 8 January 2026. If your current Skilled Worker visa was granted at B1, you can usually extend at B1.

faqs.q: Does a degree count instead of a test?
faqs.a: A degree taught in English can count. If it’s from outside the UK, you’ll need confirmation from Ecctis.

faqs.q: Will I need B2 English for ILR?
faqs.a: From 26 March 2027, most settlement applications will need B2. Until then, the level is B1 in speaking and listening.

faqs.q: What score means I’m at B2?
faqs.a: If you regularly score 18 or more out of 24, you’re probably working at around B2. Practise speaking and writing too, as they’re part of the real test.
